newsitem.title: FINLAND: Sagging forestries take Helsinki to lower close.
newsitem.headline: Sagging forestries take Helsinki to lower close.

text.p: Shares ended lower on Monday after sluggish trade, with paper stocks hit by the softer dollar and with forestry group Metsa-Serla's first quarter earnings report giving only a slight impulse to overall trade.
The HEX index ended off 0.29 percent at 2,998.08. Volume was fair at 426 million markka, almost 30 percent of it in telecom group Nokia.

Brokers said the tone this week would be set by a slate of key economic data due from the U.S. and Germany, with the focus shifting towards the U.S. Federal Reserve's May 20 open market committee meeting.
"The market has been shifting towards the view that no interest rate hike (from the Fed) is forthcoming," one said.
"The dollar's softness and the Monday mood dragged this market," another broker said, adding that U.S. paper stocks showed the way down on Friday.
Forestry group UPM-Kymmene fell 1.90 markka to 120.50 in fairly lively 46 million markka trade.

Metsa-Serla shed 0.50 markka to end at 39.00 markka after initially rising 0.50 on its report of first quarter earnings that were clearly above the median of analysts' forecasts, but within the broad range.
Trade in Metsa-Serla was lively at over 18 million markka.
Nokia failed to hold minor gains and edged down 1.00 to close at 328.50 in sturdy 130 million markka volume.
Rauma rose 1.00 markka to 116.50 in heavy 68 million markka volume, most of which stemmed from one big deal matched in-house at Enskilda at 116.00 markka per share.

Brokers said interest in Rauma remained after UPM-Kymmene's announcement last week that it would cut its stake in it to around 35 percent from 60 percent through a public placement of shares, boosting liquidity.

Raisio ended off sharply, falling 18.00 markka to 400.00, in fair 1.6 million markka volume. Dealers said the share had been fickle lately and easily swung more than 10.00 markka in either direction on a few moves by foreign investors.
